narrative.title: Charting Every Sweep Route Through the Warehouse Grid
narrative.scenario: A cleaning robot starts in the top-left bay of a square warehouse and must reach the bottom-right bay, where some bays are walled off. The robot may step up, down, left, or right into open bays, never visiting a bay twice on one route. Route control wants the complete catalogue of possible sweeps, each written as the sequence of moves taken.
narrative.inputFormat: An n x n binary matrix m (1 = open bay, 0 = blocked) and its size n.
narrative.outputFormat: Every path string of moves (U/D/L/R) from (0,0) to (n-1,n-1), sorted lexicographically by the verifier.
constraints: m[0][0] = 1 and m[n-1][n-1] = 1 for solvable grids

complexity.optimalTime: O(3^(n^2)) worst case — each open bay branches to at most three new directions
complexity.optimalSpace: O(n^2) recursion depth and visited marking

testCases.explanation: Exactly two sweeps exist: one cutting right early, one running down first.
A fully open 2x2 admits the two obvious two-step routes.

hintLevels: Level 1: The robot's only memory is the grid itself — mark the current bay blocked so a sweep can never loop back on its own trail.
Level 2: At each bay try all four moves in a fixed order, appending the direction letter; restore the bay to open when the recursion unwinds.
Level 3: The visit-mark also serves as the validity check: a move is legal only if it lands inside the grid on an open (1) bay — which automatically excludes cells on the current trail.
